constitution_lesson_output.title: 1. Why did India need a Constitution?
constitution_lesson_output.subject: History & Civics

questions.question: Arrange the key milestones in the making of the Indian Constitution in chronological order from 9 December 1946 to 26 January 1950, stating what happened on each date.
questions.answer: In chronological order: (1) 9 December 1946 — the Constituent Assembly held its first meeting; (2) 15 August 1947 — India became independent; (3) 26 November 1949 — the Constitution of India was adopted; and (4) 26 January 1950 — the Constitution came into effect, when India became a republic.

questions.question: Why did India need a Constitution after becoming independent on 15 August 1947?
questions.answer: When India became independent on 15 August 1947, it needed fundamental rules to govern the country. India was a large and diverse nation, with people belonging to different religions, languages, and communities. A Constitution establishes how a country is governed, defines the powers of government, protects citizens’ rights, and sets out principles that guide the nation.

questions.question: What is the difference between the significance of 26 November 1949 and 26 January 1950 in the making of the Indian Constitution?
questions.answer: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949, whereas it came into effect on 26 January 1950, when India became a republic and 26 January is celebrated every year as Republic Day.

questions.question: What roles did Dr. Rajendra Prasad and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar play in the Constituent Assembly during the making of the Indian Constitution?
questions.answer: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly, while Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, which prepared the draft Constitution.

questions.question: What important questions did the Constituent Assembly debate while preparing the Constitution, and how did these discussions help independent India?
questions.answer: The Constituent Assembly debated important questions including equality, freedom, minority rights, and the structure of government. These discussions helped shape a Constitution suited to an independent India.

questions.question: What system of government did the Indian Constitution establish, and what four ideals are expressed in its Preamble?
questions.answer: The Constitution established a democratic system of government, and its Preamble expresses the four ideals of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
